extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of literary travel sketches and countryside vignettes (particularly those depicting Irish/Highland rural life)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing evocative literary sketches/travel vignettes that capture rural Irish life, landscape, and local speech through sensory detail, scenes of everyday work and ritual, and lyrical observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture peasant impressions and speech
rubrics_metrics.description: "Impressions, with something of the roughness of peasant speech in them and something of the beauty... those are the things I sought to capture in this book."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to record fleeting impressions and the idiom of local speakers: small, breathless moments, colloquial turns of phrase, and the 'roughness' and beauty of peasant talk. Use snippets of folk speech, local sayings, and the cadence of oral tradition to lend authenticity and emotional weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use concrete everyday scenes to show character and society
rubrics_metrics.description: The text repeatedly renders everyday activities (turf-cutting, beetling clothes, funerals, markets, ballad-singers) as the principal material of the book's portrait of Ireland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer showing through specific, ordinary scenes (work, rituals, entertainments) rather than abstract generalizations. Small domestic or communal actions reveal social texture and character: e.g., turf-cutting practices, a country funeral procession, women beetling clothes, tinkers on the road.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground writing in sensory detail (smell, light, sound)
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated sensory notes: 'the air smells deliciously of peat', 'sunlight glitters', 'the dull boom of the surf', 'the red of the fairy-thimble', 'the purring note of a sandpiper'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vivid, specific sensory details (olfactory, aural, visual, tactile) to evoke place and mood. Examples provided include peat-smell, sunlight, surf, bird calls, and the colours of plants and rock strata. These concrete images should carry the essay's emotional resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use landscape and water as emotional/poetic catalysts
rubrics_metrics.description: "for the poets thought that the place where poetry was revealed always was upon the brink of water"; bridges and water create a 'delightful sense of space and quietness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ settings—especially water, bridges, and open horizons—as focal motifs that inspire thought and poetry. Scenes by lochs, bridges, and the sea should be used to generate reflection, lyricism, and an impression of timelessness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include local performance (song, music, gesture) to animate scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed account of a ballad-singer (lyrics, refrain, actions) and fiddlers: gestures, chants, rasping bows, stamping feet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring performances (songs, tunes, dances) into the narrative with lines of lyrics, description of bodily gestures, and audience reactions. These elements enliven scenes and reveal communal tastes and tensions (e.g., applause, mockery, police watching).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect cultural/linguistic authenticity (use of Irish and local names)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent use of Irish terms and place-names and observations that hearing children speak Irish makes one feel the language is not dead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain local language, place-names, and Gaelic phrases to authenticate setting and show continuity of culture. Use untranslated terms where they carry atmosphere, and show speakers' fluency as a cultural signifier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer showing through movement and wandering
rubrics_metrics.description: "I have the swallow-mark... that means that I must always be going journeys..."; 'To lie on one's loin in the sun is all very well, but walking is better.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use travel, walking, and wandering as organising devices: moving through landscape produces discoveries, impressions, and narrative incident. Walking scenes are privileged moments for noticing and reflecting; wandering yields material for sketches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use landscape to modulate time and mood (space, quietness, timelessness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Passages stress open horizons, bridges, and sea giving a 'delightful sense of space and quietness' and making one 'cease to trouble about time.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose scenes so the geography shapes temporal feeling: open country and seascapes can create a suspended, contemplative mood. Let physical expanses slow or dissolve ordinary temporal concerns in the prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privilege sensory, concrete observation over abstract aphorism
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sunlight is better than wisdom, and the red of the fairy-thimble more than painted fans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor immediate visual and sensory particulars (light, colour, small flowers) rather than abstract pronouncements. Use concrete imagery to carry thematic weight instead of explicit philosophizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance humour and pathos in portrayals of ordinary people
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenes present humour (ballad-singer's antics, tinkers' appeals) alongside dignity and sorrow (country funeral's deep feeling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray rural folk with nuance: allow comic detail and lively speech without stripping characters of dignity or emotional depth. Use contrasts (colourful behaviour vs. underlying sorrow) to create humane portraits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use precise, attentive physical detail to establish authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Minute details—how fiddlers hold their bows, the beehive-shaped 'winter-stales', a clock crawling in the dust—are repeatedly noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include small, specific mechanics of daily life and objects (tools, gestures, dress, local practices). These particulars anchor the narrative and persuade readers of its veracity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link nature and spirituality to enlarge meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: "Nature is the 'Time-vesture of God.' If we but touch it, we are made holier."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let natural description carry spiritual or transcendent overtones when appropriate. Scenes of water, light, and quiet can serve both descriptive and spiritual functions, deepening the moral or reflective dimension of sketches.
